03 · 04KNOWLEDGE & SOP
GENERAL KNOWLEDGE
Appearance Standards

A polished, professional appearance is essential in a luxury dining environment. The way FOH team members present themselves reflects the restaurant’s brand and service standards. Grooming, uniform presentation, and demeanor should exude elegance, confidence, and attentiveness at all times.

Team members should arrive on time, in full uniform, and maintain excellent grooming throughout their shift.

Uniforms, shoes, and accessories must be clean, well-maintained, and professional. Personal hygiene, fresh breath, and daily cleanliness are essential. Uniform alterations are not permitted, and mobile phones should remain off the floor and out of the kitchen.

THE THREE CHECKS
UniformFull uniform, on time, unaltered
GroomingPersonal hygiene, fresh breath, daily cleanliness
ProfessionalismElegance, confidence, attentiveness — every shift

Presenting ourselves with pride reflects the excellence of our team and our brand.

ZERO TOLERANCE
Firearms and Weapons

Firearms, weapons, and dangerous items are strictly prohibited on MILA property. Any concern must be reported to management or security immediately. Violations may result in removal and disciplinary action, up to termination. Safety is everyone’s responsibility.

SERVICE SOP
Full Hands In, Full Hands Out

Team members should never enter or leave the dining room empty-handed. Every trip you make should add value to the guest experience.

DELIVER · WHENEVER POSSIBLE

Bring items to the table whenever possible: drinks, food, utensils, condiments, anything the guest needs.

REMOVE · ON THE RETURN

On your return, clear used or unnecessary items: plates, glassware, utensils, condiments, anything no longer needed.

THE FOUR PRINCIPLES
Stay awareBe aware of all tables around you. Support the entire floor, not just your assigned section.
Check before you clearAlways confirm the guest has finished before removing anything from the table.
Keep it cleanMaintain a clean, organized table throughout the entire guest experience.
Team firstGreat service is a team effort. Help each other and create a seamless experience for our guests.

Full hands show purpose. Full hearts create memories.

Every trip should improve the guest experience.

05BAR
✎ Manager poster · tap to zoom
◎ Riviera Dining Group standard — applies at MILA, Casa Neos, Claudie and AVA, not MILA alone
BAR STANDARDS & SERVICE SPEC
Pours · Builds · Ice · Glassware · Garnish

One standard, every venue. These are the measures and methods for every straight pour and simple build. Free-pour is measured — jigger or count, never guess. Unless a recipe states otherwise, a spirit pour is 2 oz.

01 · POUR STANDARDS
Neat · 2 ozMost spirits — room-temperature small rocks glass. Cognac / Armagnac / Calvados — snifter. Grappa / amari — copita.
On the rocks · 2 ozAged spirits — double rocks glass over 1 large party cube (no party ice? small rocks glass, 3 whole Kold Draft cubes). Un-aged spirits — small rocks glass, 3 whole Kold Draft cubes.
Shot · 1.5 ozServed in a shot glass. Never discounted.
Highball · 2 oz4–5 whole Kold Draft cubes in a highball glass. Pour the spirit over the ice, then top with soda or juice.
Short pour · 1 ozOn request only — when a guest specifically requests it and we agree. Reserved for premium product, not a workaround for a cheap shot.
NON-NEGOTIABLES

Measure every pour. Jigger or precise count — 2 oz spirit unless the spec says otherwise.
Garnish is part of the build. If none is listed, none is served.
Glassware matches the serve every time — no substitutions on the line.
Ice format is the spec. Wrong ice is a remake, not a preference.
Shots are 1.5 oz and are never discounted.
One spec, every bar. A guest gets the same drink at MILA, Casa Neos, Claudie and AVA.

03 · ICE GLOSSARY
Kold DraftThe house cube — dense, slow-melting, crystal clear. “Whole pieces” means full, unbroken cubes.
CubedStandard fill of whole Kold Draft cubes. Our default for highballs and mixed builds.
Large / party cubeSingle oversized cube for aged spirits on the rocks. Slow dilution, clean presentation.
BlockSolid carved block reserved for Japanese whisky on ice.
CollinsLong spear / column ice for tall, narrow highball service.
GLASSWARE LEGEND
Small rocksNeat pours and un-aged spirits on the rocks.
Double rocksAged spirits on the rocks over a large cube.
HighballMixers, G&Ts and tall builds.
Snifter / copitaSnifter — cognac, Armagnac, Calvados. Copita — grappa and amari.
TulipAged tequila served neat — concentrates aroma to the rim.
Sake glassJapanese whisky served straight.
AP wine · shotAP (all-purpose) wine for spritzers; shot glass for the 1.5 oz pour.
THE STANDARD, IN ONE LINE

Right measure, right glass, right ice, right garnish — every drink, every venue, every shift. If any one of the four is off, it is not the RDG standard. Build it again.

Consistency is the difference between a good bar and a great group.

06WINE
✎ Manager poster · tap to zoom
WINE KNOWLEDGE
Understanding Wine: Structure, Feel & Flavor
1 · BODY
MeansThe wine’s overall weight and texture — not a flavor.
FeelsLight = delicate. Medium = rounded. Full = dense and coating.
Wordslight, silky, rounded, rich, powerful
ScaleLIGHT — MEDIUM — FULL
2 · ALCOHOL
MeansYeast converts grape sugar into alcohol; most table wines are 8–15% ABV.
FeelsHigher alcohol adds warmth, weight and fullness; excess alcohol feels hot.
Wordslight, warming, generous, powerful, balanced
ScaleLIGHT — WARMING — HOT
3 · RESIDUAL SUGAR
MeansSugar left after fermentation, measured in g/L. Dry wine has little perceptible sweetness.
FeelsAdds smoothness, richness and sweetness; softens the impression of acidity.
Wordsbone-dry, dry, off-dry, lightly sweet, luscious
ScaleDRY — OFF-DRY — SWEET
4 · OAK
MeansWine fermented or aged in oak; new and smaller barrels give a stronger signature.
FeelsBroader, rounder and smoother; oak tannin may add structure.
Wordsvanilla, toast, spice, smoke, cedar, coconut
5 · LEES AGING
MeansWine rests on spent yeast cells after fermentation; the lees may be stirred.
FeelsCreamy, soft, weighty and rounded through the mid-palate.
Wordsbrioche, biscuit, pastry, nutty, yeasty, savory
6 · ACIDITY
MeansNatural grape acids create freshness and balance.
FeelsMakes the mouth water; high acid is crisp and energetic, low acid is soft and broad.
Wordszesty, bright, tart, lively, refreshing, soft
7 · TANNIN
MeansCompounds from skins, seeds, stems and oak; most evident in red wine.
FeelsDrying and gripping like strong black tea; ranges from silky to firm or chalky.
Wordssilky, velvety, fine-grained, firm, grippy, structured
ScaleSILKY — MEDIUM — FIRM
8 · BUILD THE DESCRIPTION
Structurebody + sweetness + acidity + tannin
Flavorfruit + floral/herbal + earth/oak
Finishshort, clean, lingering, complex or powerful
ExampleMedium-bodied and dry, with bright acidity, silky tannins, dark fruit and a long savory finish.
FOH FORMULA

Structure + Flavor + Finish = a confident wine description.
